title: Microwave response of superconductors with paramagnetic impurities
summary: Dilute concentrations of paramagnetic impurities embedded in superconductors break Cooper pairs, create low-energy subgap quasiparticles that can impact the performance of superconducting microwave resonators and devices. The authors develop here the microscopic theory for the microwave response of superconductors with low-energy subgap quasiparticles and predict the low temperature Joule dissipation, anomalies in the London penetration depth, and frequency shifts of high- resonators. The authors show that microwave excitation of low-energy subgap quasiparticles gives rise to residual resistance of high- superconducting RF cavities.

title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
summary: The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem powerfully constrains the low-energy behavior of quantum many-body systems. In spin systems with spin rotation and conventional (Euclidean) lattice translation symmetries, it forbids a unique, gapped, symmetric ground state at half-odd-integer spin per unit cell. Here, the authors generalize this theorem to hyperbolic lattices — synthetic structures that emulate negatively curved space. Unlike Euclidean lattice translations, hyperbolic translations are noncommutative. By adapting a flux-threading argument, the authors derive LSM constraints on gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter.

title: Importance of nonlinear long-range electron-phonon interaction for the carrier mobility of anharmonic halide perovskites
summary: The carrier mobility in many materials is dominated by scattering of the carriers with phonons. It is often calculated using only linear, one-electron–one-phonon interaction. Here, the authors present a first-principles calculation of the mobility including the nonlinear, long-range electron-phonon interaction, for the representative halide perovskite CsPbI . It is shown that the temperature dependence of the carrier mobility decreases by about 10% due to the one-electron–two-phonon interaction, which is attributed to the strong anharmonicity and low phonon frequencies present in halide perovskites.
